# Evidence Manifest golden fixtures

These four files are real Scout Evidence Manifest v1 envelopes used as
cross-implementation golden vectors for `contracts/scout_evidence_anchor.py`.

## Provenance

They were generated by the Scout app's own builder
(`createEvidenceManifestV1` in `lib/evidence-manifest.ts`) from Scout v1 test
data, so the payload shape is exactly what the app produces. `no-experiment`
is the lane-only shape, which has no `implementationReferences`.

## Expected digests

`GOLDEN_DIGESTS` in `tests/direct/test_scout_evidence_anchor.py` is
`SHA-256(canonicalizeEvidenceManifestJson(payload))`, computed with Node's
built-in `node:crypto`. The contract must reproduce those values from the
payload alone, without ever reading `integrity.digest`:

| fixture | digest |
| --- | --- |
| `verified.json` | `041c5603ac42c99de7a0331f2e0f09ba0467b7963b76cab5aecfe9a6ddda8321` |
| `mixed-case.json` | `8d4913e76c34ee7e62441a2203e4b904f04841810a9d331b9600e6e7b50ca48f` |
| `unicode.json` | `ad7aff059bd82f8a8145b64d025ea22cf94dc389939b46d7af8d6f92f8ba7c60` |
| `no-experiment.json` | `36accee46c1cb91aff429ccfbc7edd168ff8e4cc86bd7cb8cecf67e5bf45d9ef` |

`mixed-case.json` carries mixed-case hexadecimal in
`implementationReferences` and in the verification snapshot.
`unicode.json` carries multi-byte characters, an astral-plane emoji, a NUL, a
unit separator, a DEL, quotes, backslashes, tabs and newlines in
`experimentDetails.notes`.

## Why `integrity.digest` was corrected

`integrity.digest` in these files was originally the value emitted by
`lib/sha256.ts`. That function is a hand-rolled SHA-256 which agrees with
`node:crypto` for the empty string only; for every non-empty input it produces
a different value, so the digests the current app publishes are not standard
SHA-256 even though the manifest protocol declares `algorithm: "sha256"`.

The fixtures therefore carry the standard SHA-256 digest, so they are valid
Scout manifests. The defective value is preserved as a regression vector in
`test_non_standard_sha256_digest_is_rejected`, which pins
`946544e1b7ed34791c216e16390a81b718dd4e938050653a9f5eab8246d11ac8` — the digest
the app currently computes for `verified.json` — and asserts the contract
rejects it.

`mixed-case.json`'s `implementationReferences.transactionHash` is 256
characters, so it is intentionally not a valid 32-byte hash. It is a
canonicalization vector only and is never anchored; the end-to-end
case-insensitivity test derives its own manifest from `verified.json`.
